subject: the 4 numbers that decide every deal
preheader: cap rate, cash-on-cash, dscr, and net cash flow answer different questions.
headline: Four useful rental metrics—and what they cannot decide.
body: These four metrics are useful together, but none replaces property evidence, inspection, appraisal, written loan terms, or the investor's own decision process.

Cap rate is NOI divided by purchase price. It describes the entered property economics before financing, subject to the NOI convention and assumptions used. Compare only genuinely comparable calculations.
Cash-on-cash is annual pre-tax cash flow divided by total cash invested. It describes the modeled leveraged cash return, not whether the property or deal is good.

DSCR is NOI divided by annual debt service. Compare the modeled ratio with the proposed lender's written definition and minimum. A result below a selected floor does not itself establish whether a loan exists, its pricing, or what the lender will require.

Net cash flow subtracts modeled operating costs, reserves, and debt service from income. Positive cash flow and a threshold-fitting DSCR can indicate modeled cushion, but they do not make a property a real deal or an investment recommendation.

TrueCap's free preliminary screen calculates these metrics after you paste a supported address, enter the asking price, and review the editable assumptions. Verify every material input before relying on the result.
